question.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=z-4{x}^{2}-6{y}^{2}$ that passes through the point $P(2,1,22).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2,1,22) & =22-4(2)^{2}-6(1)^{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=0.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ z-4{x}^{2}-6{y}^{2} & =0 \\ z & =4{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(2,1,22)$ is the elliptic paraboloid $z=4{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}.$
